steps.instruction: Review the available local read-only results for this exact case. This dossier has no dedicated runtime check ID; use the available documented inspection results instead. Match identity and time. An unavailable, skipped or truncated result is UNKNOWN, not negative.
steps.purpose: Separate observed host information from speculation.

steps.instruction: Optional, user-run terminal reference: getenforce. Compare enforcing/permissive status to matching audit denials. Enforcing mode alone does not prove SELinux caused a denial. Read any listed preconditions and do not paste literal example placeholders.

steps.instruction: Corroborate with a different terminal reference: journalctl -b --no-pager -n 150. Match the event time, source and device/service to the reported failure. steps.instruction: Compare the exact user, access request, denial source, sandbox scope and security policy before any permissions change. steps.purpose: Isolate the smallest reproducible failure domain.

steps.instruction: Read both original solution routes and their exact instructions, distro/scope limitations, backups and optional graphical alternative before choosing one. The user initiates any install, update, reset, firmware action or physical intervention. Never automatically execute a command or replace a source. steps.purpose: Provide actionable options without silent host changes.

steps.instruction: Repeat the original affected action (Virtual machine is very slow) after a user-chosen step, in the same relevant context. Compare fresh device/app behavior, not just an inventory command. Route A recovery criterion: Guest responsiveness and host pressure improve. Route B recovery criterion: No fresh I/O errors under a known-safe repeated task. If the result is ambiguous or the original test cannot be repeated, retain UNKNOWN. Preserve logs with private details redacted and contact vendor/service support when necessary.

solution_routes.condition: Host is overcommitted on RAM or CPU
user_steps: Shut down an unused VM normally and compare the same guest task, then adjust resource allocations conservatively.
solution_routes.verification_goal: Guest responsiveness and host pressure improve.

solution_routes.condition: Guest disk experiences I/O errors
user_steps: Back up important guest data, inspect underlying host storage, and avoid destructive disk operations.
solution_routes.verification_goal: No fresh I/O errors under a known-safe repeated task.

manual_investigation_guide84.manual_conclusion: Choose among likely causes only after comparing supporting and contradicting observations. No automatic causal proof or repair authorization.

ordinary_terminal.description: Run the exact documented diagnostic command yourself in an ordinary host terminal.
steps: Read command preconditions, output interpretation and privacy warnings.
Run it only in the intended host/user session, then compare the result to the same symptom.

universal_linux_terminal.name: Universal Linux Terminal
universal_linux_terminal.purpose: Optional help for the very same documented terminal diagnostic commands.
steps: Open Universal Linux Terminal if installed.

universal_linux_terminal.limitations: Does not diagnose physical faults by itself or automatically run any command. An ordinary terminal is equally valid.
